the metabolism of MAM to a DNA-methylating species by rat hepatic microsomes is inhibited by both 3-Me-P and 4-IP and that pretreatment of rats with these two pyrazoles results in a decrease in the level of MAA-induced DNA methylation.

the metabolism of MAM acetateto a DNA-methylating species in rat liver microsomal preparations is sensitive to inhibitionby carbon monoxide aswell asby 3-MePy and 4-IP, with 4- IP being more potent than 3-MP.

4-IP, a specific inhibitor of alcohol dehydrogenase, is more potent than 3-Methylpyrazole in inhibiting the metabolism of MAM to a DNA methylatig species by rat liver microsome, and pretreatment with 4-iodpyrazole decreases MAM acetate induced DNA methylation in rat liver and colon mucosa, but pretreatment with 2-methylpyrazolde decreases DNA methylation in liver but increases it in the colon.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

4-IP inhibits MAM acetate activation to a DNA methylator, while 3-MePO inhibits the formation of the DNA methylator, but also increases the spontaneous decomposition of the parent carcinogen to methanol and formaldehye.
3-MeO-P and 4-IP are not inhibitors of MAM acetates activation in vivo, but that they may inhibit the activation of MAM acetase in vivo.
4-IP is a more effective inhibitor of liver MAM metabolism than 3-Mep, and that 3-Mep is a more effective colon MAM metabolizing inhibitor than 4-IP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic activation of MAM to a DNA-methylating species in vivo is a microsomal process which is sensitive to inhibition of cytochrome P-450 by carbon monoxide, and by the pyrazole compounds.
the metabolic activation of MAM by liver microsomes involves the oxidation of MAM to an electrophilic intermediate which is then further metabolized to methanol and carbon monoxide.

the metabolic activation of MAM in rat liver and colon mucosa is catalyzed by different enzymes and the metabolic activation of the carcinogens by the enzymes in the colon mucosal cytosol is more sensitive to inhibition by 4-IP than that by the enzymes in liver cytosol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3-MePy is a potent inhibitor of the microsomal metabolism of MAM to a DNA-methylating species, whereas 4-IP is an even better inhibitor.
4-IP and 3-MePy are not only inhibitors of the P450 enzymes responsible for the metabolic activation of MAM but also of the P450 enzyme(s) responsible for the metabolic inactivation of MAM.
the two pyrazoles are useful in vivo tools to probe the metabolic activation of carcinogens.
